thread:
maria: Heads-up — us-west2 GPU pool (p4d) at ~95% sustained for the last 6m. Queue depth is growing and we're seeing tail latency spikes. A lot of requests hitting llama-70b-int8. Proposing either: enable cross-region spillover to eu-west1 OR fallback to llama-70b-quantized-v2 in-region. Thoughts?

ops-bot: alert: gpu_pool_saturation(us-west2) severity=warning start=1781234500 current_util=95% queue_depth=420

raj: @maria +1 on an immediate fallback option. Also think we should enforce per-tenant admission controls (reserve for premium). If we only do cross-region it'll blow egress/latency/cost.

lee: Cross-region is viable but adds ~120-160ms RTT and extra egress cost (~$0.004-0.01 per request depending on size). For streaming/chat UX, that will be noticeable. For short sync calls maybe fine. :thinking_face:

tom: Suggest fallback order: 1) same-region quantized variant, 2) cross-region same-precision, 3) cross-region quantized. That keeps cache locality if possible.

eva: Ops: quick draft policy that we can push as a short-lived experiment: 

```json
{
  "admit_policy": [
    {"tier": "premium", "reserve": 0.10},
    {"tier": "standard", "max_queue": 500},
    {"tier": "free", "rate_limit_rps": 5}
  ],
  "fallback_order": ["same-region-quant","cross-region-fp16","cross-region-quant"],
  "ip_burst_protection": {"threshold_rps": 100, "penalty_secs": 30}
}
```

This would: reserve 10% capacity for premium, cap standard queue, and short-circuit obvious bursts. We need to emit metrics: spillover_count, spillover_latency_ms, spillover_cost_usd.

maria: +1 to the reserve. Also add a short-lived hard cap per-tenant burst (single tenant >100 req/s => immediate 429 for 30s). We should log tenant id for postmortem.

raj: Add another metric: cache_miss_ratio_on_fallback. Important because KV cache warmup impacts p99 heavily if we fall to a different variant. Run an A/B for 30 minutes.

lee: Note: if we fallback to quantized variant in same region we still lose some KV compatibility (namespaces differ). That will cause cold-KV and extra generations, so p50 might be fine but p99 could spike. Need to quantify.

tom: I'll stand up a canary: 5% traffic diverted to eu-west1 with the same model (fp16) and separately 5% to same-region quantized. Collect p50/p95/p99, cost, and user-visible error rates.

maria: @sanjay (oncall) can you approve temporary cross-region egress quota bump for the canary? Need 2TB egress allowance for 1 hour.

sanjay: approved for 1 hour. I'll also open a ticket with network for priority egress path to reduce RTT where possible.

maria: OK, plan: 1) push admit_policy (reserve + burst cap) as hot patch 2) start 5% eu-west1 and 5% in-region-quant canaries 3) stream metrics: spillover_count, spillover_latency_ms, cache_miss_ratio, cost_per_spill 4) evaluate after 30m and either roll to 20% or revert. If no objections I'll push in ~5m. :thumbsup:

lee: +1, but flagging we should add a warning on Console for customers affected by cross-region to avoid surprises (latency + egress billing).

eva: I'll wire up the metrics dashboard and alert thresholds for spillover_latency > 250ms and cost_per_spill > $0.01.

raj: Also an ops note — put a soft-failover window: if spillover_latency p95 > 400ms for 2m, abort cross-region and fall back to local quantized only.

maria: Good catch. I'll include that kill-switch. Pushing admit rule now.

ops-bot: deploy: admit-policy-hotfix started by maria at 1781234580 — status: rolling (canary 1%).

maria: Thanks all — monitoring. Will post results in this thread in 30m.
